# Pre-tasks Review Checklist: Standalone Session on the Hardware

**Purpose**: Check that the requirements are complete, clear and consistent before `/speckit-tasks`.
Focus areas: console safety and recovery, several viewers, configuration and shortcuts,
applications and outputs. Depth: formal pre-tasks review; audience: the owner.
**Created**: 2026-11-02
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) (with [plan.md](../plan.md), [research.md](../research.md),
[data-model.md](../data-model.md), [contracts/](../contracts/), [quickstart.md](../quickstart.md))

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Console Safety and Recovery

- [x] CHK001 Do the spec and the contract agree on the startup failure messages? US6 asks for "one line saying it must be started from a text console", while `contracts/cli.md` defines three different lines (no seat, console not active, another program controls the display). [Consistency, Spec US6, FR-002, contracts/cli.md]
- [x] CHK002 Is it specified what the screen shows when startup fails *after* the display was taken (for example EGL or GBM fails after the first modeset)? The rule "the screen is not touched" appears only in the contract. [Gap, Spec FR-002, FR-012]
- [x] CHK003 Does "display or graphics device lost" in FR-012 conflict with US3 and FR-021, where unplugging a display is normal and RubickWay keeps running even with no display left? Is "display lost" meant as the graphics device only? [Conflict, Spec FR-012, FR-021, Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK004 Are reasons other than Ctrl+Alt+F<n> for the session becoming inactive covered: another session activated by the login manager, `loginctl activate`, or `chvt` from another console? FR-011 names only the key combination. [Gap, Spec FR-011]
- [x] CHK005 Is behaviour defined for a console switch or a session pause *during startup*, before the first frame was shown? [Gap, Spec FR-002, FR-011]
- [x] CHK006 Is the start of FR-011's "within 2 seconds" defined: from the key press of the switch back, or from the moment the console is shown? [Clarity, Spec FR-011, SC-003]
- [x] CHK007 Is it specified whether the watchdog runs during startup (seat wait up to 2 s, first modeset) and during shutdown, where destructors or the final commit could hang after the loop has stopped sending heartbeats? [Gap, Spec FR-030]
- [x] CHK008 Is the lower bound of 1 second for the watchdog timeout justified against legitimate stalls, such as the first shader compilation or a modeset retry? Is a too-small value a warning? [Clarity, Spec FR-024, FR-030]
- [x] CHK009 Is the output for an internal panic specified: one line starting with `rubickway:` like other fatal errors, or Rust's default panic message, and which exit status? [Gap, Spec FR-012, FR-017]
- [x] CHK010 Is suspend while RubickWay is paused (the user is on another console) covered by FR-029, including the return to RubickWay's console after resume? [Coverage, Spec FR-029, FR-011]
- [x] CHK011 Is it defined what happens when RubickWay is started as root: refused, or allowed with a warning? FR-002 says "without root privileges" but not what root does. [Gap, Spec FR-002]
- [x] CHK012 Does "a frozen RubickWay is ended by the watchdog" also cover a freeze while the user is on another console (no display access, no frames)? FR-030 says only that the watchdog never fires *falsely* there. [Clarity, Spec FR-030]
- [x] CHK013 Is "what the console keeps of the log" in FR-013 quantified, or explicitly left to the kernel console's scrollback? Is the final error line guaranteed to be the last line written? [Ambiguity, Spec FR-013]

## Several Viewers

- [x] CHK014 For displays already connected at startup, is "the order they were connected" (FR-018) defined: connector order, connector name, or something else? [Ambiguity, Spec FR-018]
- [x] CHK015 When the pointer moves towards a shorter neighbour at a height it does not have, is it clear whether it crosses with its height clamped, or stops at the edge without crossing? The edge case says "stops at the shorter display's edge". [Ambiguity, Spec Edge Cases, FR-018]
- [x] CHK016 Is FR-020's "the whole row centred on the origin" defined for displays of different heights: the bounding box centred, so each camera is offset vertically by half its height difference? [Clarity, Spec FR-020]
- [x] CHK017 Is it defined which viewer is active when there is no pointing device at all (the edge case keeps keyboard shortcuts working, and Mod+0 and new-window placement need an active viewer)? [Gap, Spec FR-019, Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK018 Is behaviour with zero viewers specified beyond "keeps running": where new windows open, what focus cycling and maximize do, and what happens to frame callbacks? [Gap, Spec Edge Cases, FR-021]
- [x] CHK019 Are pan, move and resize operations defined when their viewer is unplugged mid-operation, and when the pointer's viewer disappears during a drag? [Gap, Spec FR-021, FR-023]
- [x] CHK020 With a fullscreen window on viewer A, is it defined what focus cycling, Mod+0, pan and zoom on viewer B do to A's fullscreen? window-management's rule "focus cycling leaves fullscreen" predates several viewers. [Gap, Spec FR-022, Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK021 Is window-management's FR-020 (a new window while another is fullscreen opens without focus behind it) restated for several viewers: does it apply only when the *active* viewer has a fullscreen window? [Gap, Spec FR-022]
- [x] CHK022 Is the maximize view (FR-013 of window-management: "the view moves to the window at 100%") consistent with FR-022's "window's viewer": does only that viewer's camera move, and what if the maximized window then spans two viewers? [Consistency, Spec FR-022]
- [x] CHK023 Is it specified what a window being moved looks like while the pointer crosses between viewers of different zoom: does it jump at the crossing, or is it shown on both? [Clarity, Spec FR-023, US3 scenario 4]
- [x] CHK024 Is the home view of a reconnected display defined relative to the *current* rightmost viewer's home view, even when that viewer's camera has moved since? [Clarity, Spec FR-020]
- [x] CHK025 Is the pointer's position defined after the row re-flows, when a display that is *not* the pointer's is removed or added to its left? [Gap, Spec FR-021, FR-018]

## Configuration and Shortcuts

- [x] CHK026 Does the edge case "matched ... by the key at shift level 0 of the active group" conflict with nested-canvas research and the current code, which match on *layout 0* at level 0 so shortcuts stay on the same keys in every layout? [Conflict, Spec Edge Cases, nested-canvas research]
- [x] CHK027 Does "any other key press cancels a pending quit" (FR-031) include modifier keys? Releasing and re-pressing Shift or Mod between the two presses would otherwise cancel the quit. [Ambiguity, Spec FR-031]
- [x] CHK028 Is the window-management contract row "Mod+Shift+Q quits" during a move or resize updated for the two-press rule? [Consistency, Spec FR-031, window-management contracts/input.md]
- [x] CHK029 Is it specified whether a terminal combination may have no modifier at all (`F12`, `Return`), which would take that key away from every application? [Gap, Spec FR-025]
- [x] CHK030 Are combinations that differ from a built-in only by an extra modifier (for example Mod+Ctrl+Q) allowed, and is matching exact? FR-025 rejects only exact duplicates. [Clarity, Spec FR-025]
- [x] CHK031 Is Mod = Ctrl's effect on common application keys acknowledged: Ctrl+Tab, Ctrl+Q and Ctrl+0 would all become RubickWay's? Is a warning or a restriction required? [Gap, Spec FR-005]
- [x] CHK032 Is a partially set `xkb` block defined: for example `layout "ua"` with no `rules`. Do unset fields take the per-field defaults (data-model) or the whole default keymap? [Clarity, Spec FR-007, contracts/config.md]
- [x] CHK033 Does the edge case "the terminal command ... exits at once: a warning is logged" match `contracts/cli.md`, where an exit is logged only when the program fails to start? Is an immediate non-zero exit a warning? [Conflict, Spec Edge Cases, FR-028, contracts/cli.md]
- [x] CHK034 Is the terminal's working directory a requirement? It is RubickWay's own directory in the contract, which is the repository when started with `cargo run`. [Gap, Spec FR-028]
- [x] CHK035 Are duplicate nodes ("the last one wins") and unknown nodes ("ignored with a warning") part of the spec's FR-026, or only of the contract? [Consistency, Spec FR-026, contracts/config.md]
- [x] CHK036 Is it defined what happens when `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is set but relative or empty (the XDG specification says to ignore it)? [Edge Case, Spec FR-024]
- [x] CHK037 Is the warning format (`<file>:<line>: <reason>, using the default`) specified for problems with no line, such as an unreadable file or an xkb set that does not compile? [Clarity, Spec FR-026, contracts/config.md]

## Applications and Outputs

- [x] CHK038 Does `xdg_toplevel.set_fullscreen(output)` keep ignoring its `output` argument now that there are several outputs, or should it choose the viewer? The window-management contract says "output ignored". [Gap, Spec FR-022, window-management contracts/protocols.md]
- [x] CHK039 Is `wl_surface.enter`/`leave` behaviour defined while paused: do surfaces leave all outputs, or keep them? [Gap, Spec FR-015, FR-011]
- [x] CHK040 For a window shown on two outputs with different refresh rates, is it defined which presentation completes its frame callbacks (the first, every one, or a chosen output)? [Clarity, Spec FR-010, contracts/protocols.md]
- [x] CHK041 Is the behaviour for applications that *hide* the pointer specified? `wl_pointer.set_cursor` with no surface is what kitty sends while typing and games send all the time; is RubickWay's pointer still drawn over them? [Gap, Spec FR-008]
- [x] CHK042 Are the misbehaving cases for outputs complete: a client keeping a `wl_output` of a removed display and using it in `set_fullscreen`, and binding the same output many times? [Coverage, Spec Edge Cases, contracts/protocols.md]
- [x] CHK043 Is it specified what applications see for `wl_output` position (`geometry` x, y) and how it changes when the row re-flows after a hotplug? The contract gives the row position, the spec says nothing. [Consistency, Spec FR-015, contracts/protocols.md]
- [x] CHK044 Is the description for a display without EDID make and model ("Unknown") an accepted requirement in the spec, or only in the contract? [Gap, Spec FR-015]

## Non-Functional Requirements and Measurability

- [x] CHK045 Is a pointer-latency or power expectation stated, now that the software pointer redraws a display on every move (research S10), so the later cursor-plane feature has a baseline? [Gap, Spec FR-008, SC-005]
- [x] CHK046 Can "no visible stutter or tearing" (SC-005) be objectively checked, for example with a frame-time log or a count of missed refreshes? [Measurability, Spec SC-005]
- [x] CHK047 Is the time from plugging a monitor to its first frame (FR-021, 2 s) consistent with non-blocking modesets that may take several hundred milliseconds per display? [Consistency, Spec FR-021, research S5]
- [x] CHK048 Is idle CPU (under 1%) still achievable with the 1-second heartbeat timer (FR-030) and the estimated-vblank timer, and are these wake-ups acknowledged in the requirement? [Consistency, Spec SC-005, FR-030]

## Dependencies and Assumptions

- [x] CHK049 Is the assumption that Arch's libseat talks to logind without the seatd daemon validated, or stated as an assumption to check at the start of implementation? [Assumption, plan Technical Context, research S1]
- [x] CHK050 Is the assumption that the default XKB rules map Ctrl+Alt+F1..F12 to `XF86Switch_VT_*` stated, together with what happens if the configured options remove it (for example `srvrkeys:none`)? [Assumption, Spec FR-011, research S11]
- [x] CHK051 Is it stated which GPU is used when `boot_vga` is missing (non-PCI or virtual GPUs) and the first card with connectors is picked, and is that acceptable for the target machine only? [Assumption, Spec FR-016, research S4]
- [x] CHK052 Is kitty's need for software rendering (no GPU buffers yet) recorded where the acceptance checks rely on it (SC-006, quickstart Q5), now that RubickWay no longer sets `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE`? [Assumption, Spec Assumptions, quickstart]
